statement: At each odd prime, every original packet on stable C3 with nonzero ordinary first Johnson homomorphism has its full pro-l fixed subgroup equal to selected cusp inertia. There is at most one original pro-l packet class, up to cusp conjugacy, whose first Johnson map vanishes after finite descent; only that possible class remains. Along any nontrivial Kummer ray at most one parameter remains.
depends_on: A.28 all-degree reduction to Lie(t,Omega); A.24 peripheral self-adjointness and exact factor1/3; A.6 odd-prime abelian-quotient H1 calculation
notes: The tensor identity D1(Omega)=[t,Omega_A], with Omega_A nonzero for every nonzero matrix A, lets the projection Omega_A->Omega reduce the remaining kernel to the centralizer of t. No invertibility is required. The exceptional condition is explicitly zero first Johnson on an open subgroup of Delta, not only on [G_L,G_L]; this makes the torsion-free restriction and A.6 inflation argument valid. Existence, identification, and the full fixed subgroup of the possible single exceptional packet are not asserted.
